newsitem.title: LATVIA: New Latvian government sets EU goal as priority.
newsitem.headline: New Latvian government sets EU goal as priority.

text.p: The future new government of the Baltic state of Latvia set out its plans on Wednesday and said one of its key aims was preparing for European Union (EU) entry and speeding the former Soviet state's reforms.
"This (government) declaration...prepares for the EU in all fields," Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs told Reuters.
The government of six parties ranges from nationalists to left-of-centre groups and is to be led by former ecomomy minister Guntar Krasts.
The previous government collapsed after outgoing prime minister Andris Shkele, a no-nonsense businessman with no party affiliation, rowed with all the coalition parties.
Shkele was credited with giving a big boost to the reforms Latvia launched after quitting the former Soviet Union in 1991 and dragging it out of a 1995 financial crisis.
Birkavs said the government's programme was a direct response to a European Commission report, which said Latvia was not ready to start early talks on EU entry.
Of the Baltic states, only Estonia was chosen by the Commission to begin early talks.
Birkavs said the new government would aim at ensuring Latvia met the criteria so it was asked to start membership talks by an EU summit in December, which will finally decide on new members.
The government programme promises to complete privatisation by the middle of next year and stick to tough monetary policies.
A parliamentary vote to confirm the new government is to be held on August 7. The government is expected to win as its parties hold more than 60 seats in the 100-seat parliament.

Although Krasts, 39, has backing to pursue reforms and stick to strict monetary and fiscal policies, some commentators have said he may find it difficult to achieve his aims given the rainbow nature of the coalition, which may pull in different directions.
